extraction.name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
extraction.description: The Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) aims to provide clarity on how models perform on a variety of embedding tasks and thus serves as the gateway to finding universal text embeddings applicable to a variety of tasks. MTEB consists of 58 datasets covering 112 languages from 8 embedding tasks: Bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, STS and summarization. Through the benchmarking of 33 models on MTEB, we establish the most comprehensive benchmark of text embeddings to date.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
extraction.citeAs: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers. MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. arXiv:2210.07316v3, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MTEB spans 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages. MTEB unifies datasets from different embedding tasks into a common, accessible evaluation framework. MTEB incorporates SemEval datasets (STS11 - STS22) and BEIR alongside a variety of other datasets from various tasks to provide a holistic performance review of text embedding models. To further the diversity of MTEB, datasets of varying text lengths are included, grouped into three categories: Sentence to sentence (S2S), Paragraph to paragraph (P2P), and Sentence to paragraph (S2P). Some datasets are custom-made for MTEB using public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv, while others are from existing benchmarks like Reddit, StackExchange, TwentyNewsgroups, Amazon reviews, Banking77, Emotion, Imdb, MassiveIntent, MassiveScenario, MTOP, ToxicConversations, TweetSentimentExtraction, SprintDuplicateQuestions, TwitterSemEval2015, TwitterURLCorpus, BUCC, Tatoeba, AskUbuntuDupQuestions, MindSmall, SciDocsRR, StackOverflowDupQuestions, BIOSSES, SICK-R, and SummEval.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: MTEB integrates datasets from various sources including SemEval, BEIR, arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, Twenty Newsgroups, Amazon customer reviews, online banking queries, English Twitter messages, Amazon Alexa virtual assistant utterances, comments from the Civil Comments platform, tweets, Sprint community questions, Tatoeba, AskUbuntu, MindSmall, SciDocsRR, StackOverflow, BIOSSES, SICK-R, and SummEval.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The MTEB benchmark was introduced with this paper published on March 19, 2023, integrating datasets collected over various prior timeframes, including SemEval datasets from 2011 to 2022.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Paragraph to paragraph (P2P) datasets, the input text is the concatenation of the title and the abstract (e.g., ArxivClustering, BiorxivClustering, MedrxivClustering) or the concatenation of title and post (e.g., RedditClusteringP2P, StackExchangeClusteringP2P).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For custom-made clustering datasets (ArxivClustering, BiorxivClustering, MedrxivClustering), cluster labels are generated using categories given to the papers by humans.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB comes with open-source code and a public leaderboard at https://github.com/embeddings-benchmark/mteb. Datasets and the MTEB leaderboard are available on the Hugging Face Hub. The project welcomes dataset, task, or metric contributions from the community via pull requests to continue its development. Reproducibility is ensured through versioning at a dataset and software level, and an automatic submission format is available for leaderboard additions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to make selecting the right embedding model easier and simplify future embedding research, providing clarity on how models perform on a variety of embedding tasks and serving as a gateway to finding universal text embeddings.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The scale of experiments and model pre-training makes controlling for data contamination challenging. Overlap of MTEB datasets with model training datasets is ignored in MTEB scores, with the belief that these effects are insignificant when enough datasets are averaged.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include: 1. Lack of very long document datasets. 2. Task imbalance, with summarization and pair classification being underrepresented. 3. Multilinguality limitations, specifically the absence of multilingual retrieval and clustering datasets, and code datasets. 4. Focus solely on natural language applications, excluding other modalities like image content.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MTEB is designed for benchmarking and evaluation of text embedding models across a variety of tasks (Bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, STS, summarization) to understand their usability in various use cases and aid in selecting the right embedding model for future research or industry applications.
